newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia on lookout for regional railway builder.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia on lookout for regional railway builder.

text.p: Malaysia will soon start putting together a consortium to build a railway network between Singapore and China, the national Bernama news agency reported on Tuesday.
"We will start looking at what sort of international consortia have the capability of funding and implementing the project," Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik was quoted as saying.
The Trans-Asia Railway network, to run between Singapore and China's Kunming province, was approved at the annual summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in Bangkok last year.
The project was also discussed during this year's leaders' summit in Jakarta, which was held last Saturday.
Upgrades are also being planned for railways in other participating countries, but details have not been finalised.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. Malaysia was appointed coordinator of the project, which also involves China, Burma, Cambodia and Laos.
Ling said on Monday that Malaysia would appoint lead consultants to the project within a month.
He told reporters on Tuesday that the consultants should come up with recommendations on financing and other implementation aspects for the project.
He said the consultants would be given 10 months to study the economic, technical and cross-border issues of the project.
